title: RBI Repo Rate Hike: Impact on Your Home Loan EMIs
description: The Reserve Bank of India recently increased the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%. This hike directly influences the interest rates on various loans, esp.

faq.a: A basis point (bps) is a common unit of measure in finance, equal to one-hundredth of one percentage point (0.01%). So, a 25 bps hike means an increase of 0.25 percentage points.

faq.q: Will my fixed-rate home loan be affected?
faq.a: Generally, no. If you have a true fixed-rate home loan for the entire tenure, your interest rate and EMI will remain unchanged. However, if your fixed-rate period has ended and converted to a floating rate, then you will be affected.

faq.q: Can I switch from a floating rate to a fixed rate?
faq.a: Yes, many banks allow borrowers to switch from a floating rate to a fixed rate, often for a fee. However, fixed rates are typically higher than floating rates, and it's important to compare the long-term cost implications before making such a switch.

faq.q: Is it a good time to take a new home loan?
faq.a: The decision to take a new home loan depends on individual financial circumstances and market conditions. While interest rates are currently higher, if you have a stable income and a clear need, it might still be a viable option. Always consider your repayment capacity.

faq.q: How often does the RBI review the repo rate?
faq.a: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) typically meets six times a year, bi-monthly, to review the monetary policy, including the repo rate. However, they can convene extraordinary meetings if circumstances warrant.

faq.q: What is the role of the RBI in controlling inflation?
faq.a: The RBI uses various monetary policy tools, like adjusting the repo rate, to manage the money supply and credit in the economy. By raising the repo rate, it aims to make borrowing more expensive, thereby reducing demand and controlling inflationary pressures.
